name: NIST AI RMF
full_name: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

sources.title: NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
NIST AI RMF Playbook, machine-readable export
sources.publisher: NIST Trustworthy and Responsible AI Resource Center

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable subcategories whose outcome is achieved, with a partially achieved outcome counting as half. The AI RMF defines no score, tiers or maturity levels; this index is an HCG measure of progress between a Current and a Target Profile.

rules.summary: The framework is voluntary and applies to organizations of any size and sector.
rules.quote: The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic

rules.summary: An organization may apply all categories and subcategories or select the ones that suit its resources and capabilities, so a subcategory can be out of scope.
rules.quote: Framework users may apply these functions as best suits their needs for managing AI risks based on their resources and capabilities.

rules.summary: GOVERN applies across the whole of AI risk management and supports the other three functions.
rules.quote: GOVERN is a cross-cutting function that is infused throughout AI risk management and enables the other functions of the process.

rules.summary: The framework does not set risk tolerance; the organization defines its own.
rules.quote: While the AI RMF can be used to prioritize risk, it does not prescribe risk tolerance.

rules.summary: A Current Profile records how AI risk is managed today in terms of current outcomes, so an outcome can be partially achieved. In the implementation index a partially achieved outcome counts as half. This is an HCG convention: the AI RMF itself defines no score.
rules.quote: An AI RMF Current Profile indicates how AI is currently being managed and the related risks in terms of current outcomes.

rules.summary: Gaps between the Current and Target Profiles are addressed through action plans.
rules.quote: Action plans can be developed to address these gaps to fulfill outcomes in a given category or subcategory.

glossary.definition: The NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework, a voluntary set of outcomes for managing the risks of AI systems, arranged by Function, Category and Subcategory.
A person or organization that plays an active role in the AI system lifecycle, including those that deploy or operate AI.
Test, evaluation, verification and validation: the activities that check an AI system performs as intended throughout its lifecycle.
An implementation of the AI RMF functions, categories and subcategories for a specific setting; a Current Profile describes how AI risk is managed today and a Target Profile the outcomes wanted.
National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. agency that publishes the AI RMF.
